purpose: Selected primary-source reading and limits for the authored periodic controls. Execution status is recorded only in actual result/verification receipts.

sources.title: On the Use of Variable Eddington Factors in Non-LTE Stellar Atmospheres Computations
sources.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society149,65–74
sources.read_scope: Publisher title/authors/date/DOI and abstract. Establishes historical variable-factor iteration and grey example.
sources.supports: Historical attribution; not a transcription of its difference equations.
sources.unread_limit: Original scannedPDF fetch failed; original equations, full tests and non-LTE calculations are unread and must not be claimed reproduced.

sources.title: High-Order Mixed Finite Element Variable Eddington Factor Methods
sources.read_scope: Section2, PDFpp3–4: transport Eq1, moment equations Eq2, angular tensor and boundary factor Eq3, fixed-point steps. Introduction on independent spatial discretizations also read.
sources.supports: A formal angular solve, closure extraction, and separate moment solve constitute the coupled algorithm. Boundary factor belongs to inflow problems.
sources.unread_limit: No claim of full59page reading, high-order mixedFEM reproduction, curved-mesh, multigrid or scalability validation.

sources.title: A Godunov Method for Multidimensional Radiation Magnetohydrodynamics based on a variable Eddington tensor
sources.read_scope: Section3.1 algorithmStep1; Section3.4 PDFp8, equations22–23 and discussion; Section6.5 shadow-test scope description read.
sources.supports: Tensor is computed from a formal transfer solution; its quadrature moments need not equal the separately integrated moments.
sources.unread_limit: Not a reproduction of Athena, mixed-frameRHD, gas coupling, shocks or the paper shadow/cloud-ablation test.

sources.title: A Radiation Transfer Solver for Athena using Short Characteristics
sources.read_scope: Equations8–16 source/opacity/moment conventions, Section3.2 angular quadrature Eq17–19 and two-stream warning; Section3.3 Eq20 formal solution and Section3.5 boundary scope read.
sources.supports: Positive angular quadratures over S2 and angularly resolved formal transport differ from a local prescribed closure.
sources.unread_limit: Proposed Fourier formal solver is not their short-characteristics/interpolation algorithm. No multifrequency, ALI, stellar atmosphere or timing reproduction claim.

sources.title: A Family of Independent Variable Eddington Factor Methods with Efficient Preconditioned Iterative Solvers
sources.read_scope: Introduction PDFpp1–3 on independent HO/LO discretizations, finite-mesh moment differences and conservation; no numerical tables adopted.
sources.supports: Do not require HO and LO moments to be identical at a fixed mesh. Their discrepancy is a discretization quantity.
sources.unread_limit: No claim of reproducing high-orderDG, preconditioner performance or large-mesh studies.

sources.title: A Two-moment Radiation Hydrodynamics Module in Athena Using a Time-explicit Godunov Method
sources.read_scope: Section2.3 PDFp5, equations11–17: localM1 tensor, trace/covariance constraints and chi(reducedflux). Introduction distinction from formalVET also read.
sources.supports: Use M1 only as a pointwise closure diagnostic here; M1 is a local algebraic model, not the formal-transfer tensor.
sources.unread_limit: No Hyperion/RHD solver or reduced-light-speed/timing validation. InstitutionalPDF endpoint returned401; arXiv original-author copy was read.

original_fixed_problem: The positive periodic Fourier-source controls and their analytic response are independently derived Atlas examples, not numerical-table reproductions of the cited papers.
algorithm_scope: A periodic FFT formal angular solve supplies closure to a separate conservative finite-difference moment solve; this is not an implementation of the cited FEM, short-characteristics or RHD schemes.
normalized_units: The angular measure is normalized to1. E=<I>, H=<Omega I>, K=<Omega Omega I>, c=1. Physical energy/flux/pressure share the stated4pi normalization; no dimensional material calibration is asserted.
reference_independence: primary.py does not import analytic reference code. Reference evaluation and distinct angular component controls assess saved primary fields.
unimplemented_scope: Time-dependent radiation, material/gas evolution and RHD
Nonlinear FLD, multi-frequency opacities and moving media
Universal AP, speedup or large3D claims
